newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian leader's supporters seek arrest in protest.
newsitem.headline: Indian leader's supporters seek arrest in protest.

text.p: Thousands of supporters of a scandal-tainted Indian politician offered themselves for arrest on Sunday in a gesture of solidarity with their jailed leader, political workers said.

Supporters of Laloo Prasad Yadav, a powerful low-caste leader who resigned on July 25 as chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, said they would continue their "fill the jails" campaign until August 7.
"The people's response is spontaneous and unexpected," said Udai Narayan Choudhary, who heads the Bihar unit of Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal party. Patna is the state capital.
Yadav was arrested and remanded in custody on July 30 for two weeks after being indicted in a $280 million embezzlement scandal. He says he is innocent.

Choudhary said about 100,000 people courted arrest on Saturday but police said only 205 were detained. "They were released late in the evening because we had no space to keep them," a police spokesman said.
"We were kept without water and food throughout the day," said party worker Ramanand Srivastava.
On Friday Yadav's supporters barricaded roads and clashed with baton-wielding policemen as the ruling party led a general strike to protest against his arrest.
Thousands of paramilitary troops were deployed in Bihar, India's second most populous state, where bad roads linking villages make law enforcement difficult.
Yadav, who ruled the economically backward state of Bihar for seven years, appointed his unschooled wife Rabri Devi as chief minister after resigning.
